title: The Mysterious World
intro: Tot unrolls a giant map of a mysterious world. There are forests, towers, villages, and a big question mark in the middle.

scenes.title: The Map Room
scenes.text: Tot unrolls a giant map of a mysterious world. There are forests, towers, villages, and a big question mark in the middle.
scenes.question: Where do you want to go first?
scenes.measures: orientation style - how the student enters new material

options.text: The tall tower - I want to see everything from the top before deciding
The forest - it looks interesting and a little mysterious
The village - there might be people there who can tell me what's going on
Straight to the question mark - that's obviously the most important place

scenes.title: The Riddle Stone
scenes.text: A large stone blocks the path. Words appear on it: "I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish. What am I?" Tot says you can answer, skip, or ask for a hint.
scenes.question: What do you do?
scenes.measures: help-seeking threshold and frustration tolerance when stuck

options.text: Think hard and try to answer myself
Ask Tot for a small hint first
Ask Tot to just tell me the answer so we can move on
Sit with it for a while - the answer will come

scenes.title: The Lantern
scenes.text: The villagers want to teach you how they make their famous glowing lanterns.
scenes.question: How do you want to learn?
scenes.measures: learning sequence preference - how new skills should be introduced

options.text: Watch someone make one from start to finish first
Just hand me the materials and I'll figure it out
Tell me the steps, then I'll follow them one by one
Make one together with someone guiding me as I go

scenes.title: The Storyteller
scenes.text: An old woman offers to tell you about the mysterious world. She can tell it three ways.
scenes.question: Which do you pick?
scenes.measures: preferred explanation format - how Tot should deliver content

options.text: As a story with characters and drama
As a map with explanations for each place
As a list of the most important facts
Just answer my questions as I ask them

scenes.title: The Wizard's Riddle
scenes.text: The wizard asks the group a riddle and you think you know the answer.
scenes.question: What do you do?
scenes.measures: confidence expression and risk tolerance around being wrong publicly

options.text: Shout out my answer right away
Raise my hand to share it
Wait to see if anyone else answers first
Stay quiet and keep it to myself

scenes.title: The Wrong Answer
scenes.text: Someone answers confidently - and gets it completely wrong. The wizard gently corrects them.
scenes.question: How do you feel watching this?
scenes.measures: relationship to failure and mistakes - how Tot should handle wrong answers

options.text: Relieved it wasn't me
Curious why they thought that
Feel a little bad for them
Glad - mistakes help everyone learn

scenes.title: The Library
scenes.text: The wizard's library has thousands of books. He says you can take one to help on your journey.
scenes.question: Which do you pick?
scenes.measures: resource preference - what kind of content they naturally reach for

options.text: A book of maps and diagrams of the world
A book of stories about travellers who came before
A book of answers to the most common questions
A book that asks you questions and fills in based on your answers

scenes.title: The Companion
scenes.text: Tot asks if you'd like a companion for the rest of the journey.
scenes.question: What kind of companion do you want?
scenes.measures: desired relationship with Tot - directly shapes persona and interaction style

options.text: Someone who knows the way and can guide me
Someone to figure things out with together
Someone who asks me questions to help me think
I'd rather go alone - I like my own pace

scenes.title: The Question Mark
scenes.text: You finally reach the question mark. Behind the door is a room full of things to learn. You can only pick one to start with today.
scenes.question: Which do you pick?
scenes.measures: learning motivation - why they study, which determines how Tot frames tasks

options.text: Something I've always been curious about
Something that will actually be useful to me soon
Something I've been struggling with and want to fix
Something I already know a little about and want to go deeper

scenes.title: Tot Asks
scenes.text: Before you go in, Tot turns to you and asks: "What should I never do when I'm helping you?"
scenes.question: What should Tot never do?
scenes.measures: communication aversions - hard constraints for every future interaction

options.text: Talk too much - just get to the point
Skip the explanation - I need to understand why
Make it feel like a test - keep it relaxed
Be too serious - make it fun
